newsitem.title: USA: NYS seen facing $3.3 bln budget gap in fiscal 1998.
newsitem.headline: NYS seen facing $3.3 bln budget gap in fiscal 1998.

text.p: New York State likely will face a $3.3 billion budget gap in fiscal 1998, based on a so-called baseline budget, the Citizens Budget Commission said on Thursday.

A baseline budget -- a financial plan that estimates future receipts and spending assuming current policies -- is mandated for the federal government and New York City, but the state has never published one.

The civic group projected that spending would grow 5.5 percent between fiscal years 1997 to 1998 to $35.8 billion, while receipts would fall 5.5 percent to $31.8 billion, producing the $3.3 budget gap.

While the state's economy is expected to expand modestly, receipts are seen dropping $1.8 billion because of the loss of non-recurring or one-time items reflected in the fiscal 1997 budget. The decline will also reflect tax cuts that have been previously approved.
At the same time, spending increases of $1.8 billion are expected in the areas of Medicaid, education aid, debt service, state operations and general state charges.

The specific increases for those programs were estimated at $529 million for Medicaid, $503 million for education aid, $421 million for state operations and general state charges, and $240 million for debt service.
